commits.subject: Test InfluxDB chunk decoding failures without a failure consumer

findings.body:
### 🔵 Needs a closer look Intentional cancellation during a blocked MessagePack read can still produce erroneous failure telemetry. **No open issues** 🎉
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Suppress telemetry for canceled blocked MessagePack reads `instrumentation/​influxdb-2.4/​javaagent/​src/​main/​java/​io/​opentelemetry/​javaagent/​instrumentation/​influxdb/​v2_4/​InfluxDbQueryState.java:59` [Javaagent] Canceling a blocked MessagePack chunk read still produces failure telemetry. In influxdb-java 2.14 and 2.25, `MessagePackTraverser` wraps read `IOException`s in `InfluxDBException`. The chunk-processor advice passes that wrapper here, so this guard saves it despite cancellation; `endResponse()` then retains it through `callbackError`, producing an ERROR span and error-tagged duration. Recognize this specific wrapped read failure as well as direct `IOException`s, while leaving decoding failures and separately captured user-callback exceptions intact. Add a MessagePack regression that cancels while a chunk read is blocked.
1 resolved since last review - [Add regression test for chunked-query decoding failure capture](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20703#discussion_r4320869073)
Review effort: Balanced

Splits the InfluxDB changes from #20685, correcting query outcomes and duration timing without changing other integrations.

- **Error classification:** Classify HTTP-200 top-level and per-statement errors with bounded `error.type`, never raw error text. Retain available HTTP error codes.
- **Terminal completion:** End asynchronous and chunked operations exactly once after callbacks and chunk processing finish, retaining callback, transport, and decoding failures, including newer-client decoding failures without a failure consumer.
- **Cancellation and compatibility:** Make the call available before failure consumers run so pre-response cancellation remains successful. Preserve `DONE` handling, callback parent context, and supported 2.4 APIs.
- **Regression coverage:** Cover synchronous response errors, one asynchronous statement error, successful and failed chunked completion, cancellation before and after response delivery, callback failures after cancellation, and a single 2.4 statement-error case, with span and duration-metric assertions. Retain HTTP `400` assertions in the existing failing-query integration test.
metadata.title: Fix InfluxDB query error classification and async completion
